what: ingest record for the Gaia ASTROMETRIC catalogue siril's config already pointed at
why_this_record_exists: siril's config set catalogue_gaia_astro to a file that did not exist, while CLAUDE.md's Environment section claimed 'Local Gaia catalogs at ~/.local/share/siril/siril_catalogues/ (astro + SPCC xpsamp chunks)'. The astro half was absent, so -cat=localgaia had nothing to read. The config was RIGHT and the file was MISSING; the config was not changed.

catalogue.name: Siril Astrometry Catalogue extracted from Gaia DR3
catalogue.rename_note: the published basename differs from the config's expected basename; the file was renamed, NOT the config. The functional probe below is what proves the rename is harmless.

hash_chain.summary: TLS -> Zenodo API md5 -> published sidecar sha256 -> payload, with the DECOMPRESSED file independently verifiable against its own published sidecar.
hash_chain.closes_the_aug09_gap: aug09's ingest can only be self-verified (a DESTINATION hash). This one is checkable against source-published hashes at every step, including the decompressed artifact, so the bunzip2 step is verified too rather than trusted.
zenodo_hash_kinds: md5 per file in the record API
sha256 sidecar files inside the record itself

step_1_sidecars_vs_api_md5.note: the sidecars carry the payload hashes, so the sidecars themselves must be verified first or a corrupted sidecar would pass a corrupted payload

step_4_reverified_at_installed_path.note: re-hashed AFTER the move, at the config's path, so a bad move cannot pass as a good download

functional_probe.why: a verified hash proves the BYTES, not that siril can read the file under a different basename. Probe rather than assume — this rig has three commands (tilt, inspector, conesearch) whose help documented a capability they do not have.
functional_probe.verdict: the installed catalogue is READ AND USED. -cat=localgaia now has something to read.
functional_probe.scope_limit: this is a REGISTERED STACK, not a raw trailed frame. It is NOT evidence against the standing finding that siril's internal solver cannot match ultra-wide TRAILED-star fields; that class was not tested here.

not_changed.siril_config: catalogue_gaia_astro was already correct and was left untouched
not_changed.CLAUDE.md: the stale Environment claim is in the owner's file; flagged, not edited

REPRODUCIBILITY_GAP_STILL_OPEN.finding: this catalogue is installed but NOT rebuildable from tracked files, which is the condition CLAUDE.md's Environment rule exists to prevent.
REPRODUCIBILITY_GAP_STILL_OPEN.root_cause: x86_bootstrap.sh never fetched the astrometric catalogue. It installs the SPCC photometric chunks (layer B2) and sets catalogue_gaia_photo, but nothing fetches gaia_astrometric.dat or verifies its presence. So a fresh rig gets a config pointing at a file the bootstrap never creates, and no verify step fires.
REPRODUCIBILITY_GAP_STILL_OPEN.why_this_record_is_not_in_manifest_tsv: manifest.tsv is GENERATED, not hand-maintained: x86_bootstrap.sh line 135 truncates it (`: >"$MANIFEST"`) and rewrites the header on every --go run. A hand-added row would survive in git until the next bootstrap and then vanish silently — recreating this same bug in a new form.
REPRODUCIBILITY_GAP_STILL_OPEN.the_fix_that_would_close_it: a fetch + manifest + verify step in x86_bootstrap.sh alongside the existing layer B2 SPCC block, pinned to the sha256 in this record. NOT APPLIED — a build-path script change, out of scope for an ingest task and left for scoping.

SECOND_FINDING_five_of_six_configured_ca.note: measured while verifying this one; the astro catalogue was not the only gap

measured.catalogue_gaia_astro: PRESENT (this record; was ABSENT before it)

SECOND_FINDING_five_of_six_configured_ca.consequence: any command defaulting to a LOCAL NOMAD falls back to the remote service or fails. pcc's help states the remote NOMAD can be forced 'if installed locally' — locally it is not installed. Relevant to any catalogue-referenced photometry route.
